source_gaps: Pages were read through WebFetch summaries. The Apple page title was not returned, so the title uses the section name. The Apple Settings path is stated for iOS 26 only, so it carries that version. Samsung Smart Call and the Samsung Messages app are not included because no fetched step covers them. source_refs.title: Block a phone number, contact, or email within your apps (title not confirmed by WebFetch)
source_refs.section: Block a phone number, contact, or email within your apps: Phone
source_refs.applicability: iPhone and iPad with the Phone app
source_refs.verified_excerpt: The blocked caller can still leave a voicemail, but you won't get a notification.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On iPhone: Open the Phone app and tap Recents. Tap the phone number or contact you want to block, or tap the Info button (in Classic view). Scroll down and tap Block Caller. The blocked caller can still leave a voicemail, but you won't get a notification. Messages sent or received from the blocked contact won't be delivered. The blocked contact isn't notified that their call or message was blocked.
source_refs.extraction_method: WebFetch of the official page on 2026-11-17; steps paraphrased from the Phone section; the excerpt is quoted from the fetch result; apostrophes straight; no other edits.

source_refs.title: Block a phone number, contact, or email within your apps (title not confirmed by WebFetch)
source_refs.section: Use Settings to manage Blocked Contacts in iOS 26
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Messages sent or received from the blocked contact won't be delivered.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On iPhone with iOS 26: Open the Settings app. Tap Privacy & Security. Tap Blocked Contacts. Tap Add Blocked Contact, then enter the number or contact. Tap Block Contact.

source_refs.title: Block or unblock a phone number - Phone app Help
source_refs.applicability: Android phones using the Google Phone app; some steps need Android 6.0 or later
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Some of these steps only work on Android 6.0 and up.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Android: Some of these steps only work on Android 6.0 and up. Open the Phone app. Tap More, and then Call history. Tap a call from the number you want to block. Tap Block / report spam. Blocked callers cannot leave voicemails if visual voicemail is on.
source_refs.extraction_method: WebFetch of the official page on 2026-11-17; steps paraphrased from the section 'Block a number'; the excerpt is quoted from the fetch result; apostrophes straight; no other edits.

source_refs.title: Block a phone number or contact on your Galaxy phone
source_refs.section: Blocking contacts via the Contacts app
source_refs.applicability: Galaxy phones; the page says the phone should run Android 9.0 (Pie) or later
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Blocked contacts will remain in your Contacts list but won't be able to reach you.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Samsung Galaxy: The phone should be a Galaxy phone with Android 9.0 (Pie) or later. Open the Contacts app and tap the contact. Select More, tap Block contact, then tap Block to confirm. Blocked contacts will remain in your Contacts list but won't be able to reach you.

source_refs.title: Block a phone number or contact on your Galaxy phone
source_refs.section: Blocking numbers via the Phone app
source_refs.applicability: Galaxy phones; availability may vary by carrier, software version and phone model
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Availability may vary based on your wireless service provider, software version, and phone model.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Samsung Galaxy: Open the Phone app, tap More options, then tap Settings. Tap Block numbers, enter the number, and tap Add (the plus sign). Availability may vary based on your wireless service provider, software version, and phone model.
